//: Known Chrome/Edge incompatibilities that exist today. tests/compat.test.mjs fails on any violation NOT listed here, and also fails on any entry here that no longer matches — so this file cannot drift from reality. Milestone 2 deletes entries as it ports each area. Keys are '<file>::<ruleId>'.

background.js::onMessage-promise-return.reason: The ~110-case router at background.js:5082 returns Promises. Chrome ignores them, so every handler resolves to undefined. Must call sendResponse and return true. Gates the entire port.

background.js::sidebarAction.reason: background.js:114 calls sidebarAction.toggle(). Chrome has sidePanel.open() with no toggle, and loses gesture context across the preceding await.

background.js::menus-namespace.reason: browser.menus is Firefox-only; Chrome exposes chrome.contextMenus. The chrome build already requests the contextMenus permission.

background.js::menus-onShown-refresh.reason: menus.onShown + menus.refresh keep the toolbar checkboxes in sync just before paint. Neither exists in Chrome; replace with eager contextMenus.update driven by storage.onChanged.

background.js::getSecurityInfo.reason: Firefox-only TLS inspection at background.js:390. Chrome has no equivalent, so the DNS tab's TLS panel must fall back to #tls-note, which popup-dns.js:103 already handles.

background.js::webRequest-blocking.reason: background.js:404 registers onHeadersReceived with ['blocking','responseHeaders'] purely so getSecurityInfo works. Chrome MV3 forbids blocking; dropping it keeps the responseHeaders capture intact.

background.js::originUrl.reason: background.js:491 matches its own trace fetch via details.originUrl. Chrome calls this details.initiator; unported, every Chrome trace times out after 12s.

background.js::moz-extension-scheme.reason: Same line as originUrl — the scheme check must accept chrome-extension:// on Chromium.

popup.js::getViews-sidebar.reason: popup.js:7 detects sidebar mode via extension.getViews({type:'sidebar'}), which is Firefox-only and returns [] on Chrome — silently disabling the follow-active-tab block. Replace with the ?view=sidepanel marker the chrome manifest already sets.

popup-redirects.js::onMessage-promise-re.reason: False positive. popup-redirects.js:377 is a fire-and-forget listener for the redirectUpdated broadcast — it never needs to reply, so having no sendResponse is correct on both browsers.
